Senate President Godswill Akpabio has laid the foundation stone for the construction of science laboratories by the National Agency for Science and Engineering Infrastructure at Independence High School, Essien Udim Local Government Area, Akwa Ibom State. Akpabio, who performed the ceremony on Monday at his hometown in Ukana, Essien Udim LGA, said the project was a major step towards building Nigeria’s scientific and technological sovereignty, assuring Nigerians that the prevailing socio-economic challenges would soon give way to growth and development for all, especially the vulnerable poor. He vowed to rally the National Assembly to align with the Presidency towards effective implementation of key empowerment policies of the federal government. He said, “President Bola Tinubu is currently renewing the hope of our independence. There is a solemn covenant between a government and its people; a covenant greater than political parties, and more sacred than the privileges of public office. “It is that power shall serve the people, authority shall advance their welfare, and leadership shall be judged not by the splendour of its promises, but by the substance of its achievements.” Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources He noted that NASENI has become one of the institutions delivering on the mandate of galvanising government policies and programmes in favour of ordinary citizens, in line with the Renewed Hope Agenda of the Tinubu-led Federal Government. ‎“I commend NASENI and its Executive Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Khalil Halilu, for demonstrating that government can be a helping hand to the struggling, a ladder to the aspiring and a bridge between the poverty of today and the prosperity of tomorrow,” he said. ‎According to Akpabio, Democracy is not vindicated by magnificent offices or eloquent declarations; it is vindicated when the farmer prospers, when the artisan earns an honest living, when the unemployed acquire productive skills and when the poorest child can look towards tomorrow with hope.” ‎“That’s the social contract; that is the duty of leadership and the work of the government. And that is the noble work NASENI advances here today,” he stressed. ‎Speaking on the historic nature of Independence High School, he said its founders understood that freedom without knowledge would remain an unfinished victory. ‎“In 1960, Nigeria won political independence. But what is the worth of political independence if a nation remains dependent upon others for its technology, machinery, scientific knowledge and economic opportunities? ‎“Our fathers raised the flag of political sovereignty. We must raise the standard of scientific and technological sovereignty. The first independence gave us a nation. The next must give us the power to build a greater nation. ‎“That is the significance of today’s groundbreaking for laboratories in Biology, Physics and Chemistry. We are not merely laying foundations of concrete and steel. We are laying foundations for discoveries not yet made, inventions not yet imagined, scientific theories not yet propounded, and industries not yet born. ‎Earlier in his opening remarks, Halilu, who flagged off the NASENI Sustainable Empowerment Programme and the groundbreaking for STEM Laboratories in Ikot Ekpene Senatorial District, explained that the facility became necessary to alleviate poverty in society. ‎‎”Think of a farmer who has to stop processing her harvest because a machine has broken down and there is nobody nearby who can repair it. Also, think of a student who can explain how an electric circuit works but has never had the chance to build one. “Both remind us what practical training can change. It can help someone keep a business running today, and it can give a young person the confidence to build something tomorrow,” he said. ‎‎He, therefore, commended President Tinubu and the Senate President for continued commitment to the well-being of the people by backing investments in practical skills and science education. ‎‎The highlight of the event was the presentation of starter packs to 500 beneficiaries who participated in hands-on training in 13 engineering trade areas, including solar installation and electronics repair, welding, refrigeration and CNG vehicle conversion. Emem Julius
